defects: tsum f sums over the domain type of f (ℝ), not over ℕ as in the gold's ∑' (n : ℕ), f n — since f : ℝ → ℝ is not summable over the uncountable index set ℝ, tsum f is a completely different (junk-valued) object, not the intended infinite sum over natural numbers
hf_nonneg (∀ x, 0 ≤ f x) requires non-negativity on all of ℝ, not just on (N-1, ∞) as in gold's nonneg hypothesis — an unjustified strengthening/change of hypothesis
hf_antitone (Antitone f) requires antitonicity on all of ℝ, not just on [N-1, ∞) as in gold's AntitoneOn f (Ici (N-1)) — an unjustified strengthening/change of hypothesis

Uses Set.Ioo (N - 1 : ℝ) ∞ for both the integrability domain and the integral, but ℝ has no literal '∞' element (no OrderTop instance), so this does not correspond to Mathlib's Set.Ioi (N - 1 : ℝ) used in the gold and likely fails to typecheck or means something other than the intended open ray
